offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 23rd of 32.
offence.blurb: They threw more often than anyone last season, but that was under the previous staff — Mike LaFleur now takes charge, with Jacoby Brissett throwing to Trey McBride and Marvin Harrison Jr., and a running back taken third overall to feed.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 29th of 32.
defence.blurb: Getting to the quarterback is the clear shortfall, with Josh Sweat and Darius Robinson leading a pass rush that seldom arrives; the young corners Will Johnson and Denzel Burke are now under new head coach Mike LaFleur.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 30th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chad Ryland was among the most accurate kickers in the league, so whatever holds this group back is happening elsewhere — Devin Duvernay handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 24th of 32.
offence.blurb: They run a little more than most teams do, built around Bijan Robinson on the ground and Drake London and Kyle Pitts as targets, with Tua Tagovailoa throwing behind long-serving tackle Jake Matthews.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 19th of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that hunts the quarterback hard — only one team recorded more sacks — and takes the ball away often, with A.J. Terrell the established name in the secondary.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 24th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Veteran Nick Folk handles the kicking and has been reliable on field goals; rookie Zachariah Branch, a third-round pick, is the man returning kicks.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 11th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built on the run more than any other team last year, with Derrick Henry carrying and Lamar Jackson himself a major runner, though new head coach Jesse Minter inherits those tendencies rather than setting them.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 18th of 32.
defence.blurb: Plenty of famous names up front in Trey Hendrickson, Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell, yet the sacks did not come last season; Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins hold the corners under new coach Jesse Minter.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 12th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Young kicker Tyler Loop, a sixth-round pick, made a high share of his field goals, with Rasheen Ali returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 4th of 32.
offence.blurb: Everything runs through Josh Allen, who carried the ball himself more than most running backs do, and they score on the ground as well as anyone; Joe Brady has been promoted to head coach.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 12th of 32.
defence.blurb: Bradley Chubb and Ed Oliver lead a front that did not pile up sacks, while Christian Benford and first-round rookie Maxwell Hairston man the corners under newly promoted head coach Joe Brady.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 8th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Tyler Bass was one of the surest field goal kickers in the league, and running back Ray Davis doubles up on kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 27th of 32.
offence.blurb: An offence built around first-overall pick Bryce Young, with Chuba Hubbard carrying and 2025 top-ten pick Tetairoa McMillan the newest target. They gained little per pass attempt and scored few rushing touchdowns.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 15th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that takes the ball away at a decent clip but rarely gets to the quarterback, with few sacks all year. Derrick Brown anchors the line and Jaycee Horn leads the secondary.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 22nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Ryan Fitzgerald was reliable on field goals, hitting better than four in five, while fourth-round rookie Trevor Etienne handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 9th of 32.
offence.blurb: They ran the ball efficiently and almost never gave it away — fewer turnovers than any team. Caleb Williams is a real part of the running game himself, with young pass-catchers Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland around him.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 23rd of 32.
defence.blurb: A ball-hawking group that forced more turnovers than anyone in the league, though the pass rush led by Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo produced few sacks.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 18th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Cairo Santos was accurate on field goals, making better than five of every six, with rookie Zavion Thomas returning kicks.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 12th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-happy offences in football, throwing far more than the typical team, with Joe Burrow feeding Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for plenty of touchdowns. The running game does little.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 30th of 32.
defence.blurb: A defence that gets after the quarterback less than most, built on young first- and second-round secondary picks in Dax Hill and DJ Turner II alongside Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe up front.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 9th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Evan McPherson, a fifth-round pick of Cincinnati's, made close to nine in ten field goals, with Charlie Jones handling kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 31st of 32.
offence.blurb: Todd Monken takes over, so last season's numbers — the fewest yards per pass in the league — belong to the previous staff. The pieces are strikingly young: Quinshon Judkins, Harold Fannin Jr., KC Concepcion and rookie tackle Spencer Fano.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 14th of 32.
defence.blurb: Last year's heavy sack total came before Myles Garrett was traded to the Rams, and Todd Monken now takes charge, so the pass rush should look different. Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell hold up the corners.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 10th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Undrafted kicker Andre Szmyt converted close to nine in ten field goals, with Malachi Corley returning kicks under new head coach Todd Monken.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 7th of 32.
offence.blurb: A passing team a little more than most, running through Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, with Javonte Williams carrying the ball; most of their touchdowns came through the air.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 32nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that rarely takes the ball away and doesn't get to the quarterback often, built around interior linemen Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark plus corner DaRon Bland. Veteran pass rusher Von Miller has agreed to a one-year deal.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 16th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Brandon Aubrey is the centrepiece, making field goals at nearly the best rate in the league, with KaVontae Turpin handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 14th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw more than most teams, but in short bites — few teams gained less per pass — and Bo Nix is a real part of the run game with his own carries alongside J.K. Dobbins.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 3rd of 32.
defence.blurb: No team sacked the quarterback more often, led by Zach Allen and Nik Bonitto up front with Pat Surtain II in coverage, though they seldom force turnovers.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 14th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Wil Lutz was among the most accurate kickers in the league, and Marvin Mims Jr. handles the returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 5th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built around Jared Goff throwing to Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta with Jahmyr Gibbs running behind Penei Sewell; they scored plenty both ways and gave the ball away less often than most.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 22nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A group whose strength is the pass rush, with Aidan Hutchinson leading one of the league's best sack totals, while takeaways come less often. D.J. Reed and rookie Keith Abney II play the corners.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 27th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Bates handles the kicking and Jacob Saylors the kick returns; the field goals go in at a decent clip, the rest of the phase less so.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 16th of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning teams in the league, handing off to Josh Jacobs, though when Jordan Love does throw the ball travels a long way, and they rarely turn it over.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 11th of 32.
defence.blurb: Micah Parsons, a first-round pick of Dallas's, headlines a front that didn't produce many sacks last season, and the group takes the ball away about as seldom as anyone.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 23rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Rookie sixth-round pick Trey Smack does the kicking, with Skyy Moore returning kicks.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 13th of 32.
offence.blurb: Built around C.J. Stroud and Nico Collins, with a running game that gains little per carry and rarely reaches the end zone. Its clearest strength is ball security — few offences gave the ball away less.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 2nd of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that gets after the quarterback through Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter and takes the ball away as often as almost anyone, with Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 6th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking is the calling card, with Ka'imi Fairbairn making almost everything he tries; rookie third-rounder Jaylin Noel handles kick returns.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 8th of 32.
offence.blurb: Runs through Jonathan Taylor, who helps make this one of the league's best offences at scoring on the ground, with Daniel Jones throwing to Josh Downs and rookie tight end Tyler Warren.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 21st of 32.
defence.blurb: Takes the ball away at a decent clip, with Sauce Gardner — a fourth overall pick of the Jets — and Charvarius Ward covering and Laiatu Latu rushing off the edge.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 2nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Blake Grupe misses almost nothing from placekicking range, and Anthony Gould handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 6th of 32.
offence.blurb: Trevor Lawrence is a big part of the running game himself, carrying the ball far more than most quarterbacks, and the team scores plenty of rushing touchdowns despite gaining little per carry. Brian Thomas Jr. is the main target.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 8th of 32.
defence.blurb: Takes the ball away about as often as any defence in the league but seldom gets to the quarterback, despite Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen on the edges. Travis Hunter, the second pick in 2025, features too.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 13th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Cam Little, a sixth-round pick, does the kicking accurately, with running back Bhayshul Tuten doubling up on kick returns.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 21st of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most pass-heavy offences in the league, well above the league norm, with Patrick Mahomes also carrying the ball a fair bit himself and throwing to Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 6th of 32.
defence.blurb: Rarely pressures the quarterback and forces very few turnovers, and it just traded away All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Rams for four picks, leaving L'Jarius Sneed and rookie first-rounder Mansoor Delane in coverage.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 15th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking runs through Harrison Butker, a seventh-round pick who converts at a high rate, with Nikko Remigio returning kicks.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 20th of 32.
offence.blurb: A throwing offence — few teams put the ball in the air more often — built around Justin Herbert, second-year receiver Ladd McConkey and rookie back Omarion Hampton, with Herbert himself running a fair bit. Scoring on the ground was rare.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 9th of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that gets its hands on the ball, among the league leaders in takeaways, with veteran pass rusher Khalil Mack, a fifth overall pick back in 2014, still the name up front.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 5th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Built on kicker Cameron Dicker, who made a higher share of his field goals than anyone in the league, with Derius Davis handling kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 1st of 32.
offence.blurb: An offence that threw more touchdown passes than anyone, splitting run and pass right at the league average, with Matthew Stafford feeding Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and Kyren Williams carrying the ground game.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 10th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass rush that piled up sacks and a secondary that forces turnovers, and it just got two enormous additions: Myles Garrett in a trade from Cleveland and cornerback Trent McDuffie from Kansas City.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 28th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Harrison Mevis has been accurate on field goals, with sixth-round pick Jordan Whittington returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 32nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Klint Kubiak is in his first year as head coach, so last season's pass-heavy, hard-to-run profile belongs to the old staff; expect the ball to run through rookie back Ashton Jeanty and tight end Brock Bowers, behind a line that just paid Tyler Linderbaum a record deal.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 25th of 32.
defence.blurb: A new head coach in Klint Kubiak takes over a unit that neither sacked the quarterback often nor forced many turnovers last year, with Kwity Paye and young corner Darien Porter among the pieces.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 25th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Matt Gay handles the placekicking and receiver Tre Tucker doubles as the kick returner, under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 25th of 32.
offence.blurb: Jeff Hafley is new as head coach, so last year's run-leaning, ball-losing habits came under the old regime; the ground game is quietly efficient through De'Von Achane, and Malik Willis was signed to start after Tua Tagovailoa was released.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 24th of 32.
defence.blurb: Under new head coach Jeff Hafley, a young front led by 2024 first-rounder Chop Robinson and a very inexperienced pair of cornerbacks.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 4th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Riley Patterson made almost all his field goals, and Malik Washington doubles as receiver and kick returner, with Jeff Hafley now in charge.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 26th of 32.
offence.blurb: A group built around Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson that struggled to move the ball through the air and gave it away more often than any other team. Kyler Murray has now been named the starter ahead of J.J. McCarthy.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 7th of 32.
defence.blurb: Built on pressure — few teams got to the quarterback more often, with first-round pick Dallas Turner leading the rush, and they take the ball away at a decent clip too.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 3rd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Everything runs through kicker Will Reichard, who made a higher share of his field goals than anyone in the league last season, with Myles Price handling kick returns.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 2nd of 32.
offence.blurb: Gained more yards per pass than any other team, with Drake Maye also a real part of the running game on his own legs. A.J. Brown arrives by trade from Philadelphia to headline the receivers.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 4th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that leans on its cornerbacks, Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, rather than the pass rush — sacks and takeaways were both hard to come by.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 19th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Rookie kicker Andy Borregales was among the most accurate in the league on field goals; Kyle Williams, a third-round pick, handles kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 28th of 32.
offence.blurb: Throws more than most teams, partly because the running game gained less per carry than almost anyone. Young quarterback Tyler Shough works behind a line fronted by Kelvin Banks Jr., with Chris Olave the main target.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 16th of 32.
defence.blurb: Gets after the quarterback well, with veteran Cameron Jordan and Chase Young up front, and a young secondary in Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 32nd of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Charlie Smyth kicks and rookie Barion Brown returns kicks; the field-goal accuracy sits in the middle of the pack and little else stands out.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 17th of 32.
offence.blurb: Scores its touchdowns on the ground more than through the air, and quarterback Jaxson Dart is a big part of the running game himself alongside Cam Skattebo. Malik Nabers is the main receiving threat.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 26th of 32.
defence.blurb: Rarely takes the ball away, so it depends on the front — first-round rookie Abdul Carter — and a cornerback pairing of Paulson Adebo and Greg Newsome II.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 11th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Ben Sauls was the most accurate on field goals in the league last season, with cornerback Deonte Banks doubling up on kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 29th of 32.
offence.blurb: A unit built around Breece Hall's running and Garrett Wilson catching passes from Geno Smith, and one that throws a little less than most teams — the ground game gained yards while the passing game managed few touchdowns.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 31st of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that rarely gets to the quarterback and almost never takes the ball away, leaning on first-round pass rusher Will McDonald IV and cornerbacks Brandon Stephens and Nahshon Wright.

specialTeams.note: Among the best in the league at kicking field goals last season — 1st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicker Jason Sanders missed almost nothing all season, the best accuracy in the league, with Kene Nwangwu handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 19th of 32.
offence.blurb: Jalen Hurts is a big part of the running game himself, carrying the ball far more than most quarterbacks, alongside Saquon Barkley. With A.J. Brown traded to New England, more of the passing work falls to DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 5th of 32.
defence.blurb: A front built around Jalen Carter and Jonathan Greenard that gets after the quarterback, with young first-round corner Quinyon Mitchell behind them; they take the ball away at a good rate.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 31st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jake Elliott was among the more accurate kickers in the league, with Will Shipley returning kicks.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 15th of 32.
offence.blurb: Aaron Rodgers throws to two big targets in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., though the passing game did not produce many yards per attempt; Jaylen Warren carries the ball.

defence.note: Middle of the league for points allowed last season, 17th of 32.
defence.blurb: A disruptive group: few teams sacked the quarterback or forced turnovers more often, with Cameron Heyward and Alex Highsmith up front and Joey Porter Jr. at cornerback.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 20th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chris Boswell handles the kicking, with rookie fourth-round pick Kaden Wetjen returning kicks.

offence.note: Among the best in the league for points scored last season — 3rd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-leaning teams in the league by play calls, yet when Sam Darnold does throw, almost nobody gains more per attempt — largely through Jaxon Smith-Njigba, with Zach Charbonnet carrying.

defence.note: Among the best in the league for points allowed last season — 1st of 32.
defence.blurb: A pressure-and-turnover unit under Mike Macdonald, anchored by Leonard Williams inside and cornerback Devon Witherspoon, who has just been kept on a four-year, $132m extension; Terrion Arnold has also been signed for a year.

specialTeams.note: Middle of the league at kicking field goals last season, 17th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Jason Myers was one of the most accurate kickers in the league, and Rashid Shaheed doubles as the kick returner.

offence.note: Better than most for points scored last season, 10th of 32.
offence.blurb: A passing group built around Brock Purdy throwing to George Kittle, Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans, with plenty of touchdowns through the air; running the ball, even with Christian McCaffrey, gains very little per carry.

defence.note: Better than most for points allowed last season, 13th of 32.
defence.blurb: A front that almost never reaches the quarterback — no team managed fewer sacks — and doesn't force many turnovers either, leaning on young first-rounder Mykel Williams and corners Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green.

specialTeams.note: Better than most at kicking field goals last season, 7th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Kicking is the strength here: Eddy Pineiro was the most accurate field-goal kicker in the league, with Isaac Guerendo handling kick returns.

offence.note: Middle of the league for points scored last season, 18th of 32.
offence.blurb: A fairly even run-pass mix around Baker Mayfield, who carries the ball himself a good deal, with Bucky Irving running and Chris Godwin and rookie first-rounder Emeka Egbuka catching.

defence.note: Below average for points allowed last season, 20th of 32.
defence.blurb: A unit that takes the ball away as often as almost anyone while getting to the quarterback at a fairly typical rate, with young corners Zyon McCollum and Benjamin Morrison behind Yaya Diaby.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 21st of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Chase McLaughlin is reliable from distance on field goals; Kenny Gainwell handles the kick returns.

offence.note: Among the worst in the league for points scored last season — 30th of 32.
offence.blurb: They throw about as often as any team in the league, yet gain less per pass than nearly all of them, with first overall pick Cam Ward at quarterback and Tony Pollard running.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 28th of 32.
defence.blurb: A pass rush led by Jermaine Johnson and John Franklin-Myers gets home reasonably often, but the group very rarely takes the ball away from opponents.

specialTeams.note: Below average at kicking field goals last season, 26th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Joey Slye handles the kicking and rookie draft pick Chimere Dike returns kicks.

offence.note: Below average for points scored last season, 22nd of 32.
offence.blurb: One of the most run-heavy attacks in the league, and Jayden Daniels is a big part of that himself with plenty of his own carries; they move the ball well on the ground but score less through the air, with Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs outside.

defence.note: Among the worst in the league for points allowed last season — 27th of 32.
defence.blurb: A group that gets after the quarterback at a decent rate but forces turnovers about as rarely as any defence, with young corners Trey Amos and Mike Sainristil in the secondary.

specialTeams.note: Among the worst in the league at kicking field goals last season — 29th of 32.
specialTeams.blurb: Drew Stevens does the place-kicking, with Luke McCaffrey, a third-round pick of Washington's, returning kicks.
